step1_figure.circuit_type: Two-stage fully-differential CMOS operational amplifier with CMFB and cascoded output buffer
step1_figure.description: Figure 26.33 depicts the complete two-stage fully-differential op-amp incorporating a continuous-time common-mode feedback (CMFB) amplifier and resistive-capacitive CMFB sensing network. It includes added cascode NMOS transistors in the push-pull output buffers to allow wide output voltage swing without pulling excessive quiescent current.

differential_open_loop_gain.description: Low-frequency differential voltage gain (A_OL = d(vop - vom) / d(vp - vm))

equation.explanation: Two-stage op-amp differential gain. In Fig. 26.34, the simulated peak DC derivative gain is ~360 (51 dB).
equation.assumptions: Output buffer loaded by CMFB sensing resistors (20k + 20k).

sky130_expected.calculation: First stage cascode gain ~ 30-40 V/V. Second stage gain with 20k resistive load: A_v2 ~ g_m2 * (r_o2 || 20k). For I_bias ~ 20 uA, g_m ~ 200 uA/V, giving A_v2 ~ 5-10. Overall gain A_OL ~ 200 - 400 V/V (46 dB - 52 dB), corresponding to peak derivative ~ 360 in Fig. 26.34.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Resistive loading by the 20k CMFB sensing resistors reduces output stage resistance and open-loop gain to around 300-400 (46-52 dB).

output_common_mode_voltage.description: Quiescent common-mode voltage at the differential outputs (VOCM = (vop + vom)/2)

equation.explanation: The CMFB loop drives the output common-mode voltage to match the reference voltage VCM.
equation.assumptions: Sufficient CMFB loop gain to minimize steady-state common-mode error.

sky130_expected.calculation: Reference VCM = 500 mV (as defined in netlist). The CMFB loop sets V_OCM ≈ V_CM = 500 mV.
sky130_expected.reasoning: With CMFB loop gain ~200, the output common-mode voltage settles within a few millivolts of VCM (500 mV).

cmfb_forward_gain.description: Gain from the CMFB control input VCMFB to the op-amp output voltage (dv_out / dV_CMFB)

equation.explanation: Measures how variation in VCMFB modulates the center bias current and drives the output stage common-mode level.
equation.assumptions: Both differential inputs held at common-mode voltage VCM.

sky130_expected.calculation: Text specifies CMFB forward gain is approximately 25 (about 10 times less than the differential gain).
sky130_expected.reasoning: VCMFB modulates NMOS tail current xm14, which shifts diff-amp outputs and pushes the second stage outputs downwards.

cmfb_amplifier_gain.description: Voltage gain of the error amplifier in the CMFB network (Fig. 26.28b)

equation.explanation: Gain from sensed average output vcma to VCMFB using diff-amp with current-mirror load.
equation.assumptions: Current mirror active load operated in saturation.

sky130_expected.calculation: Text derives a gain of approximately 8 for the diff-amp with current mirror load.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Diff-amp with current mirror load provides modest gain (~8) ensuring overall CMFB loop gain around 200.

cmfb_loop_gain.description: Total open-loop gain of the CMFB regulation loop

equation.explanation: Total loop gain balancing the common-mode outputs.
equation.assumptions: Linear operating region around nominal bias point.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Text states loop gain of 200 is sufficient to precisely balance outputs while maintaining stability.

quiescent_current.description: Total quiescent current drawn from VDD supply

equation.explanation: Sum of currents in all 11 branches (diff-amp, middle bias, output stages, CMFB amp) plus bias circuit.
equation.assumptions: Nominal branch current ~ 20 uA, bias circuit ~ 50 uA.

sky130_expected.calculation: 11 branches at ~20 uA + 50 uA bias generator = 270 uA.
sky130_expected.reasoning: With cascode device added to the NMOS output buffer (Fig. 26.32/26.33), current is properly regulated close to expected 270 uA.

output_voltage_swing.description: Peak-to-peak output swing range per single-ended output

equation.explanation: Cascoded output buffer swings close to power supply rails.
equation.assumptions: Output devices driven near saturation/triode boundary.

sky130_expected.calculation: For VDD = 1.8V, V_out,min ≈ 0.15 V, V_out,max ≈ 1.65 V; swing ≥ 1.4 V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Fig. 26.34 confirms outputs swing rail-to-rail (from near ground to near VDD).

unity_gain_frequency.description: Unity gain bandwidth (GBW) of the op-amp

equation.explanation: Miller compensation sets unity-gain frequency with Cc = 50 fF.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Small 50 fF Miller capacitors give high GBW in the hundreds of MHz range.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench measuring DC transfer curve, open-loop differential gain, output common-mode voltage, quiescent current, and AC frequency response.
